study type: Retrospective observational cohort study with a multiple cut-off regression discontinuity design
exposure: Women just below the diagnostic thresholds for GDM (counterfactual group)
GDM diagnosis based on IADPSG/WHO criteria
Women with GDM with BMI ≥30 kg/m2
Tight glycaemic control for gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM)
cohort: 1178 pregnant women undergoing oral glucose tolerance tests (OGTT)
finding: Tight glycaemic control in pregnant women diagnosed with GDM was associated with reduced rates of LGA newborns and caesarean sections compared to a counterfactual group, but with increased rates of neonatal hypoglycaemia, induced deliveries, and insulin usage.
mod_finding: Treatment of women with GDM with BMI ≥30 kg/m2 drove the reduction in caesarean section rates: 32.9% versus 55.9%, relative risk 0.59 (95%CI, 0.4-0.87).
